chapter: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
title: Hammond hears the Reno Club broadcasts and brings the band to New York
summary: Basie confirms John Hammond heard the band on a local station; the men from Moten's band joined him later, in New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. "The band gradually built up in quality and quantity of personnel, broadcasting from the club on a small local station. It was heard by John Hammond, who decided the band must be brought to New York."
Is that when Willard Alexander flew out?

John brought him, oh. John brought Willard out. Well, let me see now. So that's between '35 and '36. Benny Morton died in '35 and you came to New York in '36. Well, Bill, I'm going to have to ask you a sticky question.
If, between '35 and '36, Buster's band had to have broken up between '35 and '36 then?
I imagine so. Whenever it did.
I mean, because if somebody was coming over from Buster's band to your band in the Reno, --
Oh, they didn't come into the Reno with you?
Oh, they came to New York with you?
They came to New York with me, yeah.
They weren't playing with you then in Kansas City?
No, it was a long time after that thing.
